highlight.title: MCP Joins the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation
highlight.summary: <cite index='22-2,24-4'>MCP becomes a founding project of the newly created Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI with support from major tech companies. This move signals MCP's transition from experimentation to enterprise infrastructure, providing neutral governance for the protocol that has become the industry standard for connecting AI systems to external tools and data.</cite>

resources.title: One Year of MCP: November 2025 Spec Release
resources.why_now: <cite index='15-11,15-12'>MCP's first anniversary milestone coincides with a major spec release featuring parallel tool calls, task-based workflows for long-running operations, and better context control - marking its evolution from an 'open-source experiment' to the 'de-facto standard' for connecting data to LLMs.</cite>

resources.title: The 2026 MCP Roadmap
resources.why_now: <cite index='17-3,17-20,17-21'>MCP has evolved well beyond its local tool origins, with the 2026 roadmap prioritizing enterprise readiness challenges including audit trails, SSO-integrated auth, and gateway behavior as enterprises deploy MCP at scale.</cite>

resources.title: The Current State of MCP from Elastic
resources.why_now: <cite index='16-26,16-3,16-4'>Following the MCP Developers Summit in San Francisco, key technical updates include Streamable HTTP replacing SSE for better scalability and cloud infrastructure support, enabling MCP deployment on services like AWS Lambda without long-lived connections.</cite>

resources.title: AI Engineering Trends 2025: MCP Everywhere
resources.why_now: <cite index='18-10,18-15,18-25'>MCP became ubiquitous in 2025 with nearly every company adopting the protocol, making 'running an MCP server almost as popular as running a web server' - though security risks and maturity concerns remain as the technology transitions from experimental to production use.</cite>

claude_take: <cite index='17-4,17-18,28-20'>MCP's transition to Linux Foundation governance and the introduction of Working Groups signals the protocol is maturing rapidly, with the 2026 roadmap focusing on enterprise readiness and production scalability.</cite> <cite index='16-20,18-24'>In 3-6 months, expect to see OAuth 2.1 integration addressing authentication bottlenecks and security frameworks emerging to handle MCP's current vulnerabilities, as enterprises demand production-ready agentic infrastructure.</cite> <cite index='15-1,17-15,17-17'>The experimental Tasks primitive and parallel tool execution will likely stabilize, enabling more sophisticated multi-agent workflows that can handle complex, long-running operations reliably.</cite>
